deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a continuous passage of historical notes in German Kurrent script on Greek history in the 360s BC: the Theban hegemony under Epaminondas and Pelopidas. It continues from folio 103 and runs on into folio 105. It reads like lecture notes or a school exercise; the hand and genre make Gauss's own authorship doubtful, and nothing on the page links it to Lagrange despite the bundle name.

Content, line by line:
(1) After his first invasion of the Peloponnese, Epaminondas establishes himself in Messenia. He recalls the Messenian exiles and refounds the Messenian state; the marginal date is 369.
(2) He returns to Thebes because his term of command (boeotarchy) has expired.
(3) In 368 the Thebans plan a new invasion of the Peloponnese, but Athens, out of envy, breaks with Thebes and allies with Sparta.
(4) Thebes extends its authority in northern Greece. Thessaly is almost entirely under the tyrant Alexander (of Pherae). Several Thessalian cities ask Thebes for help, and in 368 an army is sent under ... The sentence continues on f.105: under Pelopidas, who defeats Alexander, takes Larissa, settles Macedonian succession affairs and brings the young Philip to Thebes as a hostage.

There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct.
errors: The page contains no mathematical steps, so there are no mathematical errors to check.
Minor historical chronology: the Athenian–Spartan alliance and the second Theban invasion of the Peloponnese are usually dated to 369 BC rather than 368.

Minor historical simplification: Larissa (on f.105) was taken by Pelopidas from a Macedonian garrison under Alexander II of Macedon, not from Alexander of Pherae. The narrative across the page break somewhat conflates the two Alexanders.
